previous_attempt_summaries.strategy_summary: Reduce the global lower bound on the number of descents of the modular-inverse permutation to a local obstruction: prove that five consecutive inverse values can never be strictly increasing. This implies that every block of four consecutive indices contains a descent. A purely combinatorial covering lemma then yields at least ceil((p-2)/4) descents, and for odd primes this equals floor(p/4), which is stronger than the required bound > p/4 - 1.

strategy_summary: Unlike the failed attempts, this strategy does not try to deduce the theorem from the bare four-block hitting property alone. It keeps the true local obstruction that five consecutive inverse values cannot be strictly increasing, adds the involutive symmetry and the forced central descent, and then uses a strengthened counting tail with an explicit separate near-centre input instead of the false ceiling identity or the insufficient old covering lemma. A separate base case p=5 is included explicitly.
